annotations.title: Break down an area's business rates

description: Counts, totals and medians for the business properties in an area, grouped by street, sector, property_type, postcode_sector, postcode, verdict or council: number of properties, total and median rateable value, median £ per m² (with n_per_m2, how many properties it is based on: per-unit and trade-valued properties are left out), verdict counts (the website's five verdicts), flagged count and share (strong_case + worth_checking, as on the overpayment map) and total indicative annual saving. Area is required. Optional filters: sector, property type, rateable value range. Up to 50 groups, sortable. Costs 2 credits.

ba_code.description: Council (billing authority) code, e.g. '5390'. Alternative to council.

council.description: Council name or part of it, e.g. 'Hammersmith' or 'Leeds'. Use instead of postcode for a whole council.

group_by.description: One of: street, sector, property_type, postcode_sector, postcode, verdict, council. How to group (default street).

include.description: Optional extra sections for the answer. The ones available are listed in the response under settings.include_supported; anything else is ignored and listed in settings.ignored. Leave out unless the user asks for something the normal answer lacks.

options.description: Optional extra settings by name. The ones available are listed in the response under settings.options_supported; anything else is ignored and listed in settings.ignored.

postcode.description: A full postcode ('W6 8DR'), a postcode sector ('W6 8') or a district ('W6').

property_type.description: Words from the Valuation Office description, e.g. 'shop'.

sector.description: One of: car_parking_and_storage, healthcare, industrial_and_warehousing, leisure_and_hospitality, offices, other_specialist, retail.

sort.description: One of: properties_desc, total_rv_desc, total_saving_desc, flagged_desc, flagged_share_desc, median_rv_per_m2_desc. Default properties_desc. flagged_desc / flagged_share_desc rank by strong_case + worth_checking.
